meta.title: GPT Grammar/ASR Review — Verification & Verdict
meta.description: Independent verification of the external Earley/ASR robustness review, alignment score, and a reshaped adoption plan

props.title: The ChatGPT grammar review holds up
props.subtitle: Every code claim we spot-checked is accurate. Adopt the costed-alternative scanner contract; reshape the phonetics step; park the lattice.

props.content: We asked an external model how to make the Earley template grammar survive real Whisper output. Its answer — a staged, costed input-alternative design instead of more grammar rows or fuzzy matching — is the right architecture, and its reading of our code is flawless: 15 of 15 seam claims verified against the actual files, down to line numbers. We score alignment 8.5/10 and recommend GO on the first three steps as written, a cheaper reshape of the phonetics step, and a hard park on confusion-network/lattice parsing. One lever it underweights: decoder-side context biasing, which our channel-conditioned-decoding ruling already sanctions.

VERDICT
props.title: Adopt, reshape, park, add
props.subtitle: Per-step disposition instead of a 7-step pre-commitment. Each step keeps its pinned kill-test; a missed threshold is a successful NO-GO.

props.title: ✅ Adopt as written
props.content: Step 0 (freeze denominators, grouped folds, N-best oracle), Step 1 (zero-diff scanner refactor: multi-alternative, variable-span terminal scanning), Step 2 (top-5 N-best parse wrapper, gated on the oracle). The scanner seam is real: TerminalMatch already carries span/cost/op, but the chart advances position+1 and throws the span end away. Fixing that is a structural no-op today and unlocks everything later.

props.title: 🔧 Adopt reshaped
props.content: Step 3 (sparse learned confusions) becomes an extension of the governed substitution rule that already exists — per-pair cost, directionality, and provenance added to the current equivalent-sets mechanism, shipped as a generated hashed asset under modules/authority. Step 5 (catalog phonetics) becomes offline-generated pronunciation variants per facility/airport/fix entry, committed as a reviewable governed asset; runtime stays a table lookup. No runtime G2P or phone-distance engine unless the offline table demonstrably falls short.

props.title: 🅿️ Park indefinitely
props.content: Steps 6–7 (word confusion networks, full lattice parsing). These are Kaldi-world moves: Whisper has no honest word posteriors, its beams collapse toward the same text, and its hallucinations correlate across beams. Building graph-column chart parsing for 32 frozen eval rows cannot pay for itself. Reopen only if live-lane telemetry shows recoverable mass that N-best provably misses.

props.title: ➕ Add: decoder context biasing
props.content: The review's biggest gap. We control the Whisper decode, and the aircraft knows its own callsign, region, and route — the channel-conditioned-decoding ruling already says to use that intelligence. Per-scenario prompt/hotword biasing (own callsign, regional facilities and fixes) attacks proper-noun garble at the source, ahead of any parser-side phonetics. A repo-wide search finds zero prompt or hotword biasing anywhere today — the lever is completely unexplored. Live lane and future capture waves only; frozen fixtures cannot be retro-biased (a recapture is a new receipt under fixture law).

props.content: Calibration note: the prompt we sent pre-encoded the hard constraints (no corpus-verbatim rows, no ML in the accept path, zero-lexical-evidence law survives, kill-test-per-step). So the review echoing those laws is compliance, not insight. Its *original* contributions are the exact seam inventory above, the two-channel scoring rule (decoder score never enters the repair budget), the grouped-fold mining procedure, the staged thresholds, and a do-not-build list that matches our own gate law. Those are the parts worth paying for, and they check out.

props.label: PUSHBACK
props.title: Five places we disagree or sharpen
props.subtitle: None of these reverse the GO. They change sequencing, cost, and where the win actually lands.

props.title: 1 · The eval prize is 32 rows
props.content: The garble lane owns 32 of 289 triaged remaining losses (~11%). Bigger lanes (fragment row forms: 67, missing template rows: 44, channel/advisory: 40) are cheaper data work. The honest justification for this program is the live demo — real ASR garbles every day and that surface is unscored. Decide the roadmap on live-lane value; expect to stop at the sparse-confusion or catalog-variant step once the frozen 32 are substantially recovered.

props.title: 2 · The mined pairs share one lineage
props.content: It is worse than the review feared: all 1,544 minable pairs are ONE synthetic voice (Kokoro am_adam — the fixture TTS uses a single voice for every speaker and scenario) decoded greedily by one frozen model. Its 'require ≥2 independent groups before discounting' rule is structurally unsatisfiable from fixtures alone — a mined confusion may encode the fixture voice, not radio reality. The real transfer tests are the frozen BATC held-out set and live captures. No pair gets priced below the generic substitution cost until it appears in a second lineage.

props.title: 3 · Whisper is not Kaldi
props.content: The review's trust hierarchy ('decoder posterior alternatives are strongest evidence') assumes calibrated lattice posteriors. Whisper gives sequence logprobs over beams that collapse toward similar text, and it hallucinates fluently under radio noise — correlated across beams. Worse: our deployed TensorRT decode is GREEDY today — the config declares beam_size 5 / best_of 5, but the backend factory never passes params and the backend hardcodes beam_size=1. So 'expose the top-5' means implementing beam/temperature decode in the TensorRT lane (or a matched-weights sidecar for the oracle), not flipping a flag. The oracle must run the same finetuned model family we deploy (jacktol whisper-large-v3 ATC finetune).

props.title: 4 · Half the machinery already exists
props.content: Governed pair-level substitution is live today: for↔four↔4 ships as an equivalent set, and chain→change already passes the 0.72 similarity gate at cost 0.35. The tokenizer already joins letter-spellings (G-O → go), leaving exactly the 'routin g' residue the review targets. So the sparse-confusion step is a schema extension (per-pair cost, direction, provenance, generated asset), not a new mechanism — and the remaining twin failures are fusions/splits, budget exhaustion, and proper nouns, which is precisely where the plan's later steps aim. The diagnosis is right; the build is smaller than it looks.

props.title: 5 · Frozen-fixture law applies to N-best
props.content: Our ASR eval lanes consume frozen 1-best transcripts; exporting top-5 hypotheses is a new fixture artifact, which under fixture law means a new receipted capture wave (procedure + blob hashes in the receipt), not an edit. Also: all measurement routes through `just baseline` (extend the scoring scripts, never fork), the oracle tooling belongs next to the existing ASR tools, and the compound-composition invariants bucket joins the gate list because variable-span consumption can shift split boundaries.

props.content: Sequencing stays oracle-first: the step-0 experiment decides whether the correct words even exist in the decoder's alternatives. If they do, N-best recovers rows with zero relaxation of terminal acceptance. If they don't, no amount of parser-side fuzz can manufacture acoustic evidence — that is the review's own logic, and it is correct.

props.content:
Yes — with the reshapes above. The review's core insight is exactly right for this codebase: the parser doesn't need more grammar rows or a fuzzy-match predicate, it needs a richer *input representation* fed through the existing priced-repair discipline. The scanner seam it identified is real and half-built already. Its staging (prove the acoustic path exists before building machinery to exploit it) mirrors our own gate law.

What we bring that it couldn't: the frozen-fixture and receipt governance, the single-voice lineage of the mined pairs, the fact that pair-level governed substitution already ships, the greedy reality of the deployed decode, and the channel-conditioned-decoding ruling that makes decoder biasing the cheapest unexplored lever.

Independent of the verdict, verification surfaced one latent bug to file on its own: the transcription config declares beam_size 5 / best_of 5, but the TensorRT backend factory drops the params and the backend hardcodes greedy decode — the config is currently aspirational (config/base.yaml:36-50 vs modules/transcription/backends/factory.py:74-77 and backends/tensorrt/backend.py:55).

Recommended commitment: steps 0–1 now (analysis + zero-diff refactor, no behavior change), then let the oracle result and the live-lane demo value decide how far up the ladder to climb. WCN and lattice parsing stay parked unless live evidence — not eval ambition — demands them.

props.title: Scoring breakdown
props.content: Code-reading accuracy 10/10 · architecture soundness 9/10 · house-law fit 9/10 (prompt pre-encoded much of it) · repo practicality 7/10 (fixture law, lineage, existing pair machinery missed) · lever-space completeness 7.5/10 (decoder biasing underweighted). Overall: 8.5/10 — GO with reshaping.
